Mounts to pneumatic chair lift — moves with chair height adjustments automatically, no repositioning needed
360° swivel rotation — encourages natural leg movement for active sitting and improved circulation
14" non-slip textured platform — secure foot positioning with or without shoes
280 lb weight capacity — heavy-duty steel construction for long-term reliability

Swivel: 360° full rotation
Weight capacity: 280 lbs
Construction: Heavy-duty steel with powder-coat finish
Surface: Non-slip textured
Required base: 26″ nylon base
Compatible pneumatic lifts: 157mm, 200mm, or 267mm
Installation: Tool-free, 5–10 minutes
Color: Black

Country of Origin: Canada
Warranty: 5-year limited warranty
Who Benefits from the ERGOFP?

The 360° Foot Platform is ideal for anyone whose feet don't comfortably reach the floor when seated at proper desk height, or who wants active sitting benefits from dynamic foot movement. It is especially beneficial for:
Shorter users (under 5'6") who cannot reach the floor at proper desk height
Sit-stand desk users who adjust chair height throughout the day
Users experiencing leg numbness, swelling, or poor circulation from dangling feet
Anyone seeking active sitting benefits without a floor-based footrest
Workstations with limited floor space where a floor footrest is impractical
Users who move their chair frequently and need foot support that moves with them
How to Install the ERGOFP
Confirm your chair has a 26″ nylon base and a compatible pneumatic lift (157mm, 200mm, or 267mm)
Lower your chair to its lowest height position
Open the mounting clamp and position it around the pneumatic gas cylinder

The Science Behind Keyboard Ergonomics
Frequently Asked Questions
Will this fit my desk?

The Humanscale keyboard tray mounts under most standard desks using a clamp or grommet mount. Confirm your desk thickness and underside clearance before ordering. Our specialists can advise on compatibility for non-standard configurations.
What's the difference between the 900 and 950 platform?

The 900 is a standard-width platform suitable for most keyboards. The 950 is a wider platform designed for larger keyboards or users who prefer more surface area. If you use a full-size keyboard with a number pad, the 950 is recommended.
What's the difference between the standard and high mouse platform?

The standard 90 mouse platform positions the mouse at the same level as the keyboard. The 90H (high) mouse platform raises the mouse slightly, which can benefit users who prefer a higher mouse position relative to the keyboard.
Does negative tilt really make a difference?

Yes — significantly. Negative tilt (keyboard angled slightly downward away from you) keeps wrists in a neutral, straight position rather than extended upward. This is the clinically recommended keyboard angle for preventing carpal tunnel syndrome and wrist strain.
How difficult is installation?

Most installations take 15–20 minutes with basic tools. The system clamps or mounts to the underside of your desk. Detailed instructions are included. Our specialists can also provide guidance if needed.
Is this suitable for corporate bulk deployments?

Yes — the Humanscale keyboard tray is one of the most widely deployed ergonomic accessories in corporate environments. For bulk orders, volume pricing, or workstation assessments, contact our certified ergonomic specialists.
Can I use this with a standing desk?
Yes, when the standing desk is in its seated position. The keyboard tray mounts to the underside of the desk surface and moves with it as the desk adjusts height.

How to Adjust Your Goldtouch Elite for Maximum Comfort
The Elite's dual-adjustment system lets you customize both tenting (vertical angle) and splay (horizontal angle) to match your unique body and workspace:
Tenting Adjustment (0–60°):
0–10° (minimal tenting): Good starting point for ergonomic keyboard beginners or very low desk setups
20–30° (moderate tenting): Most popular range—eliminates pronation for most users without feeling extreme
40–60° (aggressive tenting): Maximum pronation relief for RSI recovery, standing desks, or users with severe wrist pain
Adjustment tip: Start at 20° and increase gradually over 2–3 days until you find your sweet spot
Splay Adjustment (0–30°):
0–10° (minimal splay): Best for narrow shoulders or compact desk spaces
15–20° (moderate splay): Ideal for average shoulder width—most users land here
25–30° (maximum splay): Perfect for broad shoulders, tall users, or those who want maximum ulnar deviation relief
Adjustment tip: Set splay so each keyboard half aligns directly with its shoulder—your forearms should be parallel
Separation Distance: The Elite's split design allows up to 6" of separation between halves. Position them shoulder-width apart to eliminate internal shoulder rotation and reduce upper back tension.

Frequently Asked Questions
How long does it take to adjust to the split layout?

Most users adapt within 2–3 days. Start with minimal tenting (10–15°) and gradually increase over the first week. Your typing speed may decrease slightly for the first 1–2 days but typically returns to normal or improves within a week as the ergonomic positioning reduces fatigue.
Is the Goldtouch Elite good for carpal tunnel syndrome?
Can this keyboard help with wrist pain, tendinitis, or RSI?
Is this keyboard good for herniated disc or neck pain from poor posture?
Can I use this keyboard for gaming?

Yes, the Goldtouch Elite works for gaming, though it's optimized for typing and productivity. The membrane switches provide quiet, responsive feedback suitable for strategy games and MMOs. For competitive FPS gaming requiring rapid WASD movement, traditional gaming keyboards may be more suitable.
Will this work with my standing desk?

Absolutely. The adjustable tenting is perfect for standing desks—increase the tenting angle when standing to maintain neutral wrist position at the higher desk height. Many users keep two angle settings: 20–25° for sitting, 35–45° for standing.
Do I need to remove the palm supports?

It's personal preference. Many ergonomists recommend removing them to encourage a floating-hand typing position that prevents wrist extension. However, if you prefer cushioned support, the soft-touch palm rests are designed to provide comfort without forcing harmful wrist angles.

Measure your hand from wrist crease to tip of middle finger. Small (6.5–7"), Medium (7–7.5"), Large (7.5–8"). When in doubt, choose the LARGER size — the hand-shaped design requires full contact to eliminate gripping.
Will this work if I've tried vertical mice without success?

Yes. Many users who still experience pain with vertical mice find relief with the HandShoe because it eliminates gripping entirely. Vertical mice improve wrist angle but still require gripping to control the mouse. The HandShoe addresses the root cause of mouse arm — gripping strain.
How long does it take to adapt to the HandShoe Mouse?

Most users adapt within 2–3 days. Start with 30–60 minute sessions and gradually increase. Cursor precision returns within 1–2 days — faster than vertical mice because the HandShoe maintains traditional mouse orientation. Pain relief typically begins within the first week.
Is this available for left-handed users?
Yes. The HandShoe Mouse is available in dedicated left-hand models designed specifically for left-handed users' anatomy — not a compromised ambidextrous design.
Should I choose wired or wireless?
Choose wired for zero-latency precision work (graphic design, CAD, video editing). Choose wireless for cable-free flexibility and clean desk aesthetics (general office work, presentations).
Can I use this for gaming?

The HandShoe Mouse is optimized for productivity work rather than gaming. The hand-shaped design prioritizes comfort over rapid movement. For gaming, consider a traditional gaming mouse or vertical mouse.
How does this compare to trackballs?

The HandShoe Mouse maintains traditional mouse movement (arm/wrist motion) while eliminating gripping. Trackballs eliminate arm movement but require finger/thumb manipulation. Choose HandShoe if gripping is your primary issue; choose trackball if arm movement causes pain.

How do I know if my monitors are VESA compatible?

How do I route cables through the cable management channels?

How Half-QWERTY One-Handed Typing Works:
Revolutionary Typing Technology:
The Half-QWERTY system is a patented technology that allows you to type with one hand using the same QWERTY touch-typing muscle memory you already know. Here's how it works:
Normal typing: Type letters on your active hand's side of the keyboard normally
Mirror typing: Hold the Space bar and type the mirror position for letters on the opposite side
Muscle memory transfer: Your brain automatically mirrors your existing typing patterns
No relearning required: If you can touch-type with two hands, you can learn Half-QWERTY in hours, not weeks
Example: To type "hello" with your right hand:
H - Type normally (right side of keyboard)
E - Hold Space + type mirror position
L - Type normally
L - Type normally
O - Type normally

What is negative tilt and why does it matter?

Negative tilt slopes the keyboard away from you (front higher than back), which keeps your wrists in a neutral position instead of extended upward. This eliminates wrist extension—a primary cause of carpal tunnel syndrome and typing-related pain.
Does this keyboard work with RollerMouse?

Yes. The Balance Keyboard is specifically designed to pair with Contour RollerMouse devices. The compact, centered layout positions perfectly in front of a RollerMouse for the ultimate ergonomic setup that eliminates both wrist extension and shoulder reaching.
What's the difference between the wired and wireless versions?

Both versions have identical ergonomic design and features. The wired version (102106) connects via USB for reliable, always-on connectivity. The wireless version (102104) uses Bluetooth for cable-free flexibility. Choose based on your desk setup and connectivity preference.
Will this work with my Mac?
Yes. The Balance Keyboard is compatible with both Windows and Mac operating systems. It works plug-and-play without drivers or software installation.
How long does it take to adjust to the split layout?

Most users adapt within 2-3 days. The Balance Keyboard uses a standard QWERTY layout with a moderate split—less extreme than some ergonomic keyboards. Start with short typing sessions and gradually increase usage as you adapt.
Can I use this keyboard without a RollerMouse?

Absolutely. While the Balance Keyboard pairs perfectly with RollerMouse devices, it works excellently as a standalone ergonomic keyboard with any mouse. The split design and negative tilt provide ergonomic benefits regardless of your pointing device.
What is the key travel distance?
The Balance Keyboard features low-profile keys with reduced travel distance compared to traditional keyboards. This minimizes finger extension and reduces typing fatigue during extended use.
Is the palm support removable?
The integrated palm support is built into the keyboard design and is not removable. It's positioned to provide comfortable support without forcing wrist extension.

What is the Kinesis Savant Elite2 FP10J?
Do I need to install drivers or software?

What is the FP10J factory configuration?

Out of the box: Jack 2 (Front) = left mouse click, Jack 1 (Rear) = right mouse click. The pedal included in the FP10J kit is connected to Jack 2 (front), so it performs a left mouse click by default. You can reprogram either jack to any keyboard action, macro, or mouse button.
Can I add a second pedal?

Yes. The 2-jack control module supports a second pedal or hand trigger connected to Jack 1 (Rear). Additional Savant Elite2 pedals are sold separately. This gives you two independent hands-free inputs without using an additional USB port.
What actions can I program the pedal to perform?

Any keyboard action, modifier (Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Cmd), complete key sequence (e.g., Cmd-W, Ctrl-Shift-Z), macro, or mouse click (left, right, middle, scroll). Programming is done by editing a plain text file — no coding required.
Does the Savant Elite2 work on Mac?

Yes, with some limitations. Complete key sequences (e.g., Cmd-W) work correctly. However, Mac OS X does not natively support middle mouse button without a third-party driver, and modifier actions from one USB device cannot modify input from a second USB device due to Apple OS limitations.
